title: Airport Lighting, Markings & Signs Quiz
description: Test your knowledge of airport lighting systems, visual aids, runway/taxiway markings, and airport signs from AIM Chapter 2

questions.question: What is the purpose of Approach Light Systems (ALS)?
options: To identify the runway threshold from a distance
To provide transition from instrument flight to visual flight for landing
questions.explanation: ALS provide the basic means to transition from instrument flight to visual flight for landing. They extend from the threshold into the approach area.

questions.question: How far do approach light systems extend for precision instrument runways?
questions.explanation: ALS extend 2,400-3,000 feet for precision instrument runways and 1,400-1,500 feet for nonprecision instrument runways.

questions.question: When using a 2-bar VASI, what indication shows you are on the correct glidepath?
options: Far bar red, near bar white
Far bar white, near bar red
questions.explanation: On glidepath: red over white (far bar red, near bar white). All red = below glidepath. All white = above glidepath. 'Red over white, you're alright.'

questions.question: What is the safe obstruction clearance area for VASI?
options: Full width of runway to 3 NM
questions.explanation: VASI provides safe obstruction clearance within ±10 degrees of the extended runway centerline and to 4 NM from the runway threshold.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a 3-bar VASI system?
options: To provide two visual glidepaths for high cockpit aircraft
questions.explanation: Three-bar VASI provides two visual glidepaths. The upper glidepath (middle and far bars) is ¼ degree higher, intended for high cockpit aircraft to ensure sufficient threshold crossing height.

questions.question: What are REILs and what is their purpose?
options: Red Edge Identification Lights - mark runway edges
Runway End Identifier Lights - rapid identification of approach end
Rotating End Illumination Lights - visibility enhancement
Reflective Edge Indicator Lights - night visibility
questions.explanation: REILs (Runway End Identifier Lights) are synchronized flashing lights on each side of the runway threshold that provide rapid and positive identification of the approach end.

questions.question: What color are runway edge lights on the last 2,000 feet (or half the runway) of an instrument runway?
questions.explanation: On instrument runways, yellow replaces white on the last 2,000 feet or half the runway length (whichever is less) to form a caution zone for landings.

questions.question: What color do runway end lights emit toward the runway vs. Outward?
questions.explanation: Runway end lights emit red toward the runway (indicating end to departing aircraft) and green outward (indicating threshold to landing aircraft).

questions.question: What is the color sequence of runway centerline lights starting from the landing threshold?
options: White, then alternating red/white last 2,000 ft, all red last 1,000 ft
Green at start, white middle, red at end
questions.explanation: Centerline lights are white until the last 3,000 feet. Then white alternates with red for the next 2,000 feet, and the last 1,000 feet are all red.

questions.question: What is the RWSL (Runway Status Light) system?
options: Fully automated system indicating when it's unsafe to enter/cross/takeoff/land on runway
questions.explanation: RWSL is a fully automated system that provides runway status information using REL and THL lights. It does NOT substitute for ATC clearance.

questions.question: What do illuminated red Runway Entrance Lights (REL) indicate?
options: High speed traffic on runway or aircraft on final approach
questions.explanation: Red REL lights indicate there is high-speed traffic on the runway or an aircraft on final approach within the activation area. Do not enter the runway.

questions.question: How does a pilot control airport lighting at an uncontrolled field?
options: Key the aircraft microphone a specific number of times
questions.explanation: Pilot-controlled lighting uses microphone keying: 7 clicks = highest intensity, 5 clicks = medium, 3 clicks = lowest. Lights stay on for 15 minutes.

questions.question: How long do pilot-controlled lights remain illuminated after activation?
questions.explanation: All pilot-controlled lighting is illuminated for 15 minutes from the most recent time of activation.

questions.question: What does a rotating airport beacon with alternating white and green indicate?
questions.explanation: White and Green alternating = lighted land airport. White and Yellow = water airport. Green, Yellow, White = heliport. Military = dual-peaked white flashes between green.

questions.question: What might the operation of an airport beacon during daylight hours indicate?
options: Ground visibility less than 3 miles and/or ceiling less than 1,000 feet
questions.explanation: Daytime beacon operation often indicates weather below VFR minimums (visibility <3 SM and/or ceiling <1,000 ft). However, pilots should not rely solely on this - check weather directly.

questions.question: What color are taxiway edge lights?
questions.explanation: Taxiway edge lights emit blue light. Taxiway centerline lights are green.

questions.question: What are clearance bar lights and what color are they?
options: Three in-pavement steady yellow lights at holding positions
Flashing red lights at runway intersections
questions.explanation: Clearance bar lights are three in-pavement steady-burning yellow lights at holding positions to increase conspicuity in low visibility conditions.

questions.question: What should a pilot NEVER do regarding stop bar lights?
options: Request them to be turned on
Taxi past them when cleared by ATC
Cross a red illuminated stop bar, even if cleared by ATC
questions.explanation: Pilots should NEVER cross a red illuminated stop bar, even if an ATC clearance has been given. The lights indicate it is unsafe.

questions.question: What color are runway markings?
questions.explanation: Runway markings are white. Taxiway markings, holding positions, and closed/hazardous area markings are yellow.

questions.question: What are the three types of runway markings?
options: Visual, nonprecision instrument, and precision instrument
questions.explanation: The three types are: visual (basic), nonprecision instrument, and precision instrument. Each has progressively more marking elements.

questions.question: Where is the runway aiming point marking located?
options: At the midpoint of the runway
Approximately 1,000 feet from the landing threshold
questions.explanation: The aiming point marking (two broad white stripes) is located approximately 1,000 feet from the landing threshold and serves as a visual aiming point for landing.

questions.question: What do touchdown zone markings indicate in terms of distance?
questions.explanation: Touchdown zone markings are coded to provide distance information in 500-foot increments, using groups of 1, 2, and 3 rectangular bars.

questions.question: What does an enhanced taxiway centerline (parallel dashed yellow lines) indicate?
options: Approaching a runway holding position marking
questions.explanation: Enhanced taxiway centerline (parallel yellow dashes on either side of centerline) warns pilots they are approaching a runway holding position marking and should prepare to stop.

questions.question: What do runway holding position markings look like?
options: Four yellow lines: two solid and two dashed
questions.explanation: Runway holding position markings consist of four yellow lines (two solid, two dashed). The solid lines are always on the side where aircraft must hold.

questions.question: When is an aircraft 'clear of the runway' after landing?
options: When the nose wheel crosses the holding position marking
When the main gear crosses the runway edge
When all parts of the aircraft have crossed the holding position marking
questions.explanation: An aircraft is not clear of the runway until ALL parts of the aircraft have crossed the applicable holding position marking.

questions.question: What does a mandatory instruction sign look like?
questions.explanation: Mandatory instruction signs have a red background with white inscription. They denote entrance to a runway/critical area or areas prohibited from entering.

questions.question: What does a location sign look like?
options: Black background with yellow inscription and border
questions.explanation: Location signs have a black background with yellow inscription and yellow border. They identify which taxiway or runway you are currently on.

questions.question: What does a direction sign look like?
questions.explanation: Direction signs have a yellow background with black inscription. They show designations of intersecting taxiways with arrows indicating direction.

questions.question: What do runway distance remaining signs indicate?
options: Remaining runway in thousands of feet
questions.explanation: Runway distance remaining signs (black background, white numbers) indicate remaining runway in thousands of feet. A '3' means 3,000 feet remaining.

questions.question: What does EMAS stand for and what is its purpose?
options: Emergency Marking Alert System - alerts to hazards
Engineered Materials Arresting System - stops aircraft overruns
Electronic Monitoring and Alerting System - monitors runway
Enhanced Movement Area Signage - improves navigation
questions.explanation: EMAS (Engineered Materials Arresting System) is located beyond runway ends and is designed to crush under aircraft weight to safely stop overruns. Marked with yellow chevrons.

questions.question: What is the normal VASI glidepath angle?
questions.explanation: The normal VASI glidepath is set at 3 degrees. Some locations may have angles up to 4.5 degrees for obstacle clearance.

questions.question: How far is VASI visible during day vs night?
questions.explanation: VASI lights are visible from 3-5 miles during the day and up to 20 miles or more at night.

questions.question: What is a SIDA at an airport?
questions.explanation: SIDA (Security Identification Display Area) is a limited access area requiring proper badge/identification. Movement without authorization is prohibited.

questions.question: What color are taxiway centerline lead-off/lead-on lights near a runway?
questions.explanation: Taxiway centerline lead-off/lead-on lights alternate green and yellow, warning that you are within the runway environment or ILS critical area.

questions.question: Which lights indicate the Land and Hold Short point when LAHSO is in effect?
questions.explanation: Land and Hold Short Lights are pulsing white lights installed across the runway at the hold short point. They are on only when LAHSO is in effect.
